title: Subjunctive in Fixed Expressions
summary: Recognize fossilized and idiomatic subjunctive patterns that convey concession, wish, indifference, and condition.

sections.heading: Concessive formulas
sections.body: Expressions such as **seja como for**, **custe o que custar**, and **aconteça o que acontecer** use the subjunctive to generalize over possibilities.

examples.pt: Seja como for, precisamos decidir hoje.
examples.en: Be that as it may, we need to decide today.

examples.pt: Custe o que custar, vou terminar o projeto.
examples.en: Whatever it costs, I will finish the project.

examples.pt: Aconteça o que acontecer, mantenha a calma.

sections.heading: Wishes and blessings
sections.body: Fixed wishes often use present subjunctive, sometimes without an explicit main clause. They can sound warm, formal, religious, ironic, or theatrical depending on context.

sections.heading: Indifference and choice
sections.body: Patterns like **quer você queira, quer não**, **goste ou não**, and **seja X, seja Y** express indifference to alternatives or exhaustive possibilities.

examples.pt: Quer você queira, quer não, isso vai acontecer.
examples.en: Whether you want it or not, this will happen.

examples.pt: Goste ou não, a regra mudou.
examples.en: Like it or not, the rule changed.

examples.pt: Seja por pressa, seja por descuido, o erro se repetiu.
examples.en: Whether from haste or carelessness, the error was repeated.

keyPoints: Fixed subjunctive expressions often generalize over all possible outcomes.
Que + subjunctive can express wishes without a main verb.
Concessive formulas are common in formal argument and everyday speech.
Many expressions are best learned as chunks.

commonMistakes.note: The fixed expression uses future subjunctive for.
